name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Endocrine Regulator — 'Stillwater'
description:
The Lazarus Stillwater is an implanted endocrine regulation system consisting of a primary microprocessor node implanted near the adrenal glands and a distributed network of nano-fiber sensors threaded through the circulatory system, monitoring and modulating hormonal output in real time. The system intercepts adrenal and cortisol surges — the biological substrate of fear, panic, and stress response — and either dampens them to a manageable baseline or, in a toggled mode called Flood, deliberately amplifies them in a controlled cascade that produces a sustained state of heightened physical performance without the cognitive impairment of uncontrolled adrenaline. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals developed Stillwater originally as a treatment for trauma-related stress disorders in high-risk occupational environments, and this clinical framing remains central to how it is licensed and prescribed.

What distinguishes Stillwater from crude chemical suppression — injected compounds, patch delivery systems — is its precision and reversibility. The system does not eliminate emotional response; it places the operator in control of their own biochemistry, allowing them to choose their affective state within the parameters of the system's programming. Trained users describe it as 'choosing your weather' — the ability to enter a negotiation in a state of genuine calm, survive a firefight without the tunnel vision of panic, or push through physical exhaustion by deliberately engaging Flood. The nano-fiber sensor network also provides continuous biometric monitoring, and can be configured to transmit health data to a paired device — a feature marketed to corporate wellness programs and used by intelligence handlers to monitor field operatives.

Stillwater has developed a complicated cultural reputation. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' clinical positioning emphasizes therapeutic legitimacy, and there is a genuine population of trauma survivors and high-stress professionals who use it for exactly that purpose. But the same system that stabilizes a disaster relief worker also produces operators who can commit acts of violence without physiological distress — who can interrogate, threaten, and harm with the biochemical affect of someone doing paperwork. This has made Stillwater a subject of significant ethical debate in GLMZ's regulatory bodies, none of which have successfully restricted it.

cultural_context: Stillwater sits at the intersection of medical legitimacy and operational utility in a way that makes it difficult to regulate or stigmatize. Among trauma survivors and first-responders, it is straightforwardly therapeutic. Among corporate operators and intelligence professionals, it is standard equipment for anyone who regularly sits across a table from people trying to read them. On the street, it has a darker reputation — 'Laz-ER' is associated with operators who don't flinch, people who have chemically insulated themselves from the normal human reluctance to cause harm. The ethical question of what it means to choose calm in a moment that should feel terrible is one that GLMZ's culture has not resolved.
known_users: Intelligence field operatives under handler monitoring
High-end fixers managing volatile multi-party situations
Certain combat operators who prioritize sustained performance over spike capability
story_hooks: A player's Stillwater unit has been silently transmitting biometric data to a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals research division — not their handler, not their employer. The data is being used to build a behavioral profile for a purpose that becomes clear when someone tries to buy it.

A witness to a corporate atrocity is entirely calm when describing what they saw — Stillwater calm. They don't seem traumatized because biochemically, they aren't. A player must determine whether this is a survivor coping or a perpetrator who never felt anything.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals releases a mandatory firmware update for all licensed Stillwater units. Operators who accept the update report that Flood mode now feels different — more compulsive, harder to end. Those who refuse the update find their licenses flagged.

An underground community of Stillwater users has formed around the shared experience of 'choosing your weather' — but some members have begun using it to suppress emotions they think they should feel, and are losing the ability to access them at all.
